To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a multi-factor asset pricing framework, the pricing nature of sentiment risk is not universal and it is not a priced factor in the presence of market risk premium and size, book to Market equity and momentum risk factor.

the choice of a multifactor asset pricing model is a pragmatic approach to explain the cross section of return in emerging markets, and the market wide risk factors are priced in a rational manner and not by the sentiment.

i) the unconditional multifactor model is able to capture the cross sectional variation in the average return, ii) book to market equity is not able to explain the average returns in case of large size stocks and iii) the presence of market wide sentiment risk factor does not affect the cross sectional pricing implication of other risk factors in the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pricing of sentiment risk in the context of multifactor model.
the pricing implications of sentiment risk in the context of emerging markets, and our empirical results are in line with the prior literature.
the multifactor model specification and the impact of market wide sentiment risk on cross sectional stock return.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the five factor model is a better alternative to explain the cross section of Indian stock return.
the pricing implication of sentiment in the context of emerging market is not a priced risk factor.
the choice of a multifactor model is a pragmatic approach to explain the cross section of average stock returns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the choice of five factor model is more appropriate to explain the pricing implication of risk factors in Indian stock market, and the pricing implication of market wide risk factors is more robust than sentiment risk.
the pricing of sentiment risk is a function of market structure and the presence of rational risk factors.

the five factor model is a better asset pricing model than three factor model, and the pricing implication of sentiment factor is conditional on market structure, market efficiency, and investor behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important to incorporate market sentiment as an additional risk factor along with other market wide risk factors in the multifactor asset pricing model to explain the average cross sectional stock return.
the presence of market wide sentiment risk is a priced risk factor, but its pricing implication varies with the choice of risk factors.
the pricing nature of sentiment risk in the context of India is not universal and the pricing evidence is not robust across different market conditions.
